passage:
Thursday: Zubin, five, peers at Chachi's baby asleep in the cradle. 'Why doesn't she have a name yet?' Dadi says, 'On Sunday everyone will come and give it to her.'
Sunday: Forty people squeeze into the flat. The pandit whispers into the baby's ear, and Chacha announces, 'Sharmila!' Everyone claps. Zubin tries to count the guests and gives up.
Monday: Zubin asks Mumma, 'Why did so many people come for one tiny baby?' Mumma says, 'Because she belongs to all of us now. Like you do.' Zubin leans over the cradle. 'Hi, Sharmila. I'm yours too.'

qa.q: Who announced the baby's name?
qa.a: Chacha.

qa.q: What was Zubin feeling when he asked why so many people came?
qa.a: He felt curious and a little amazed, puzzled that one tiny baby could bring so many people together.

qa.q: What did Mumma's answer give Zubin?
qa.a: A simple reason he could understand, that a baby belongs to the whole family, which helped him feel part of the welcome too.

qa.q: What would it mean for baby Sharmila to grow up with so many people at her naming?
qa.a: She would grow up knowing a big circle of family counts her as their own, just as Mumma said.

grounding: Shows a young child who watches a baby cousin's naming ceremony, asks why so many people came, and learns that a new life belongs to a wide family circle.

passage: It poured all morning on the day of baby Aamir's aqiqah, and the tent on the terrace leaked. Still people kept arriving, dripping: Khalas, Mamus, neighbours, even Jeevan Uncle from downstairs holding his umbrella over two old aunties. Asif, six, watched Chachu gently shave the baby's fuzzy hair while Dadi murmured a prayer. Aamir cried; everyone laughed kindly. Asif tugged Ammi's sleeve. 'Why did all these people come in the rain for a baby who just cries?' Ammi smiled. 'Because now he's everyone's Aamir. Same as you were.' Asif looked at the wet crowd again and stood a little taller.

qa.q: Who held an umbrella over two old aunties?
qa.a: Jeevan Uncle from downstairs.

qa.q: How did Asif feel after Ammi's answer, and what shows it?
qa.a: He felt proud and included, standing a little taller as he realised he too belongs to that wide circle.

qa.q: How did Ammi help Asif understand the ceremony?
qa.a: She answered his honest question simply and linked it to his own babyhood, so he could see what the gathering meant.

qa.q: What does Jeevan Uncle coming in the rain suggest about how the neighbours see the baby?
qa.a: It suggests the neighbours feel part of the family's joy, willing to brave the rain to welcome Aamir.

grounding: Illustrates a young child at a baby cousin's first-haircut and naming rite who asks why so many came, and learns that a life belongs to a wider circle of family, faith and neighbours.

passage:
At baby Mittu's mundan in the Rohini community hall, Manoj, five, counted people on his fingers and ran out of fingers four times.

The barber shaved Mittu's curls while Vikas Chacha held him, and Mittu howled. Everyone clapped anyway.

"Papa, why did so many people come just for a haircut?"

Papa crouched down. "It's not just a haircut. It's saying, this baby is ours. Everyone here will look after him. They came for your mundan too."

Manoj touched his own hair. "Me too?"

"You too. Your Nani cried."

Manoj looked at the crowd again, differently, then went and patted Mittu's bald head very gently.

qa.q: Who held Mittu during the shaving?
qa.a: Vikas Chacha held him.

qa.q: What did Manoj feel when he learned people had come for his mundan too?
qa.a: Manoj felt surprised and touched, seeing the crowd differently and patting Mittu's head gently.

qa.q: How did Papa help Manoj understand?
qa.a: He crouched down and explained simply that the ceremony tells everyone the baby belongs to them, linking it to Manoj's own.

qa.q: What might the day be like for Vikas Chacha?
qa.a: Vikas Chacha likely feels proud and emotional, holding the crying baby while the whole circle welcomes him.

grounding: Shows a child at a younger cousin's first-haircut ceremony asking why so many came, and learning a life belongs to a wider circle.

passage:
"Dadi, why are there so many people?" Sangeeta whispered from behind the pillar. "The baby doesn't even know them."
"Today we tell everyone her name," Dadi said. "Vishal Chacha will whisper it in her ear first. Then Pandit-ji will say it aloud."
"Why can't they just tell her at home?"
"Because a name isn't only for the baby. It's for everyone who will call her." Dadi squeezed her hand. "These people will call her name her whole life."
Vishal Chacha bent over the cradle and whispered. Then Pandit-ji said, "Anika!" and everyone repeated it.
Sangeeta tried it quietly. "Anika." Then louder, with everyone. "Anika!"

qa.q: Who whispers the baby's name first?
qa.a: Vishal Chacha will whisper it in her ear first.

qa.q: How did Sangeeta feel when she joined in saying 'Anika'?
qa.a: Sangeeta went from puzzled to excited and included, saying the name louder with everyone.

qa.q: What did Dadi do that helped?
qa.a: She answered Sangeeta's why simply, explaining that a name is for everyone who will call it.

qa.q: What might Vishal Chacha feel as he whispers the name?
qa.a: He likely feels tender and proud, giving the baby her name before the whole family.

grounding: Shows a child at a baby's naming ceremony asking why so many people came, and learning the name belongs to a wider circle.

passage:
Class note, KG-A, Monday — Bidisha

Lalit (5) came back from the weekend full of news. His baby cousin had a naming ceremony at the gurdwara, and "the WHOLE hall came, even people I don't know!"

He asked me, "Why did they all come for one small baby?"

I asked what he thought. "Maybe because she's new and they want to say hello." Close enough.

Then he drew a tiny baby surrounded by forty smiling stick people and labelled it "Everybody's baby".

What I did next: at circle time, three children shared their own family ceremonies. Lalit's picture is on the board.

qa.q: What did Lalit label his picture?
qa.a: He labelled it "Everybody's baby".

qa.q: What does Lalit's picture suggest he felt about the ceremony?
qa.a: It suggests he felt amazed and happy that so many people came to welcome one small baby.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped Lalit's understanding?
qa.a: Asked what he thought first, then let classmates share their own family ceremonies at circle time.

qa.q: How might the baby's family feel if they saw the picture?
qa.a: They would probably feel touched that Lalit understood the day as a whole circle welcoming her.

grounding: Shows a child who saw a baby cousin's naming ceremony, asked why so many came, and grasped that a life belongs to a wider circle.

passage: In the little church in Aldona village, Francis, five, sat squeezed between aunties. His baby cousin Rhea was getting her name at the font, wearing a long white dress. There were so many people: uncles from Mapusa, the neighbours, the baker, even the old fisherman. Francis tugged Sarika aunty's sleeve. "Why did so many people come for a baby?" Sarika aunty whispered, "Because now she belongs to all of us, not just her mummy and daddy." Francis looked around at all the faces. Afterwards, he held Rhea's tiny hand. "I'm your cousin," he told her.

qa.q: Where was baby Rhea given her name?
qa.a: In the little church in Aldona village, at the font.

qa.q: What was Francis feeling when he asked why so many people came?
qa.a: He felt curious and puzzled, surprised that a baby needed so many people.

qa.q: How did Sarika aunty's answer help Francis?
qa.a: It showed him that the baby belongs to a big circle of family and neighbours, which he then joined by telling Rhea he was her cousin.

qa.q: How might Rhea's parents feel seeing so many people at the church?
qa.a: They probably felt happy and supported, knowing their baby had a large circle around her.

grounding: It illustrates a child at a younger cousin's naming who asks why so many came and learns a life belongs to a wider circle.
